body.statement: There exists \(c>0\), depending only on \((d,\beta,L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)\), such that for every even \(T\ge32\) and every \(B\ge1\), \[R_T(B)\ge cF_\alpha(T,b).\] The inequality holds against every randomized policy in \(\Pi_{T,B}\).
body.justification: A weighted-suffix converse separates persistent capacity cost from the shrinking-partner deadline cost for all policies.
body.gap: Online matching lower bounds in \cite{ascheretal2026generalarrivals} and \cite{azarchiplunkarkaplan2017delays} use competitive ratios or delay adversaries and do not retain the causal scalar-oracle subtraction.
body.consumer: The converse tells investigators how much precision no reservoir implementation can recover at a specified cap.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\pi\in\Pi_{T,B}\), and write \(C_h\) for the cost in Definition \(\mathrm{def:pair\text{-}cost}\) with \(g=h\).  Draw \(h\sim\nu\) from Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:holder\text{-}variogram\text{-}prior}\), independently of the uniform covariates and \(\xi\), and use the corresponding law \(P_h\) from that lemma.  By policy nonanticipation, \(M_\pi\) is a function only of the covariates and \(\xi\), so it is independent of the draw of \(h\).  The edge sum is finite and bounded, so linearity permits the expectations and the sum to be interchanged.  The variogram inequality followed by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:weighted\text{-}suffix\text{-}geometric\text{-}lower}\) gives
\[
\begin{split}
\mathbb E_{h\sim\nu}\mathbb E_{P_h,\xi}C_h(M_\pi)
&=\mathbb E_{X,\xi}\sum_{(i,j)\in M_\pi}\mathbb E_{h\sim\nu}\{h(X_i)-h(X_j)\}^2\\
&\ge c_\nu\mathbb E_{X,\xi}\sum_{(i,j)\in M_\pi}\|X_i-X_j\|_2^{2\beta}\\
&\ge c_1T F_\alpha(T,b)
\end{split}
\]
for a constant \(c_1>0\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:offline\text{-}adjacent}\) and \(\|h\|_\infty\le A_\nu\) imply \(O_h(X)\le4A_\nu^2\) pathwise.  Since every \(P_h\) is in the model class, averaging over \(h\) and then bounding a supremum below by an average show that
\[
Q_\pi:=T^{-1}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,d}(L,G,H,\underline f,\overline f)}
\mathbb E_{P,\xi}[C_g(M_\pi)-O_g(X)]
\ge c_1F_\alpha(T,b)-\frac{4A_\nu^2}{T}.
\]
Independently, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:mandatory\text{-}final\text{-}pair\text{-}lower}\) gives \(Q_\pi\ge c_{\mathrm{end}}/T\).  Thus
\[
c_1F_\alpha(T,b)\le Q_\pi+\frac{4A_\nu^2}{T}
\le\left(1+\frac{4A_\nu^2}{c_{\mathrm{end}}}\right)Q_\pi.
\]
The multiplier is finite because \(L,G,H>0\).  The resulting lower bound on \(Q_\pi\) is uniform over every deterministic or randomized feasible policy.  Taking the infimum over \(\pi\) in Definition \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}regret}\) proves
\[
R_T(B)\ge cF_\alpha(T,b),
\]
where \(c>0\) depends only on the fixed envelopes listed in the theorem.
